Educational Information

What is a Simple Pendulum?

A simple pendulum consists of a point mass (bob) suspended from a fixed point by a massless, inextensible string. Under the influence of gravity, it exhibits periodic motion called simple harmonic motion for small angles.

Key Physics Principles:

  • The period depends only on length and gravity, not on mass or amplitude (for small angles).
  • Energy continuously converts between kinetic and potential.
  • The restoring force is proportional to displacement (Hooke's Law analog).

Small Angle Approximation:

The formula \( T = 2\pi \sqrt{\frac{L}{g}} \) is most accurate for angles less than 15°. For larger angles, the actual period is longer than predicted because the restoring force (sin θ) is noticeably less than θ itself.

Real-World Applications:

  • Pendulum clocks for timekeeping
  • Seismometers for earthquake detection
  • Foucault pendulum demonstrating Earth's rotation
  • Measuring local gravitational acceleration
